newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-VIALLI UNHAPPY WITH CHELSEA BOSS GULLIT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VIALLI UNHAPPY WITH CHELSEA BOSS GULLIT.

text.p: Former Italy international Gianluca Vialli has criticised the tactics of his Chelsea coach Ruud Gullit after three matches on the bench.
"It's not a very happy time for me," the former Juventus captain, who joined Chelsea at the start of the season, told Italian Tele+2 pay television on Wednesday evening.

"Gullit has used me very little recently and I'm not happy about that. I did not come here to have a holiday or to have fun. I came to do well, to become a legend in London at Chelsea. Being on the bench makes me frustrated, I hope things change in future. I'm not willing to put up with it much longer."
Vialli, who makes up an Italian trio at the English premier league club with internationals Gianfranco Zola and Roberto Di Matteo, was openly critical of Gullit.

"Sometimes I think that if a coach keeps the captain of the team that won the European Cup just six months ago on the bench, this must either mean that the club is top of the league -- and at the moment it isn't -- or that maybe the coach is not doing a very good job and that something is probably wrong."

Vialli, a popular hero at home and one of his country's most successful strikers, was the first of the Italians to sign for Chelsea and had looked forward to making a big splash in England after winning everything Italy had to offer.
But he has been sidelined by a hamstring problem and then overshadowed recently at Chelsea by new signing Zola from Parma, who has become a crowd favourite at Stamford Bridge.

Last week, new Italian coach Cesare Maldini signalled he wanted Zola and Di Matteo for his first match in charge -- a friendly against Northern Ireland in Palermo on Wednesday -- but not Vialli who last played for Italy in 1992.
Vialli said that despite being on the bench, "I am waiting patiently, I continue to train, trying to grit my teeth."
Italian newspapers on Thursday quoted Gullit's assistant Gwyn Williams as saying he did not think Vialli's remarks were particularly sensational.

"It's true he has not played recently but it was because he was injured. When he's recovered, he'll play again. I have no doubts. I talked to him this morning and he seemed happy, he and Gullit have an excellent understanding."
Gullit, appointed as player-manager, regularly played against Vialli when the Italian was at Sampdoria and the Dutch midfielder was one of AC Milan's top players.
The Dutchman indicated recently that he intended to keep change to a minimum in the Chelsea line-up after a recent run of strong form with Zola linking up well with Mark Hughes.
